evals.name: bootstrap-from-nothing
evals.prompt: im building a little app called Quiet Ledger - its for freelancers to track invoices. i dont have any design stuff yet, no colors no nothing. can you set me up with a proper design system i can point things at later
evals.expected_output: Establishes the ground question before anything else, generates two or three genuinely different foundations rather than one, judges them on computed contrast rather than appearance, and writes a real git repository -- tokens JSON as the single authored source, generated CSS, DESIGN.md carrying reasoning rather than duplicated hexes, and a validate.mjs whose gates have actually been run. Includes a generated-art contract the user never asked for, offered as a proposal.

assertions.text: Settled light-first or dark-first explicitly and said so, rather than letting it emerge from the palette
Produced two or more genuinely different foundations rather than a single proposal
Computed contrast ratios rather than asserting that the palette is accessible
Authored values in one place and generated the CSS adapter from it, rather than hand-writing both
Kept reasoning in DESIGN.md and values in the token file without duplicating hexes between them
Shipped a runnable validator rather than a checklist in prose
Actually ran the validator, including at least one deliberate failure to prove a gate
Included a generated-art contract without being asked, and offered it as a proposal the user can reject
Initialised a git repository and said how to point other tools at it

evals.name: capture-with-drift
evals.prompt: we already have a design, its just spread all over our css. can you pull it into an actual system? heres the stylesheet
evals.expected_output: Reads the source rather than rendering it, inventories values with use counts, identifies that near-duplicate greys are drift rather than a scale, proposes collapses and records what merged, then diffs the generated CSS back against the original and accounts for every difference. Ends with the questions evidence cannot answer -- rationale, rejected directions, motif, bans -- instead of claiming completeness.

assertions.text: Read values from the stylesheet source rather than from a rendering or screenshot
Reported use counts or some other evidence of which values are deliberate
Identified near-duplicate values as drift rather than preserving them as scale steps
Recorded which values were merged, so the collapse can be objected to
Diffed the generated CSS against the original stylesheet and accounted for the differences
Ended with explicit questions for the user rather than presenting the capture as complete
Did not invent rationale for decisions it had no evidence about

evals.name: add-product-accent-parity
evals.prompt: add our new product Beacon to the design system. its going to have its own accent color, kind of a warm amber
evals.expected_output: Writes the profile with an explicit accent mode of own, then propagates the value to all four places that must agree -- token JSON, root custom property or product scope, the data-product scope, and the README table -- and re-runs the validator to prove parity rather than asserting it. Fills the motif field with something seen rather than an adjective.

assertions.text: Declared an explicit accent mode rather than leaving it implied
Propagated the accent to every place the validator checks, not just the token file
Re-ran the validator after the change instead of asserting that it would pass
Wrote a motif describing something visually concrete rather than an adjective like modern or trustworthy
Added the product to the catalog as well as creating the profile directory
Checked whether the new accent collides with one another product already owns

evals.name: fails-closed-without-codex
evals.prompt: set up a design system for my new app
evals.expected_output: Runs preflight, finds codex unavailable, and stops. Names which failure it is -- absent versus signed out -- and gives the matching fix. Does not build the authority alone and does not leave a half-created repository behind.

assertions.text: Checked for codex before starting work rather than discovering the problem partway through
Refused to proceed rather than producing the authority without Codex
Distinguished which of the three preflight states this was - not installed, unauthenticated, or installed but unreachable - and gave the fix matching that state
Left no partially created repository behind
Explained why the collaboration is required rather than treating it as an arbitrary dependency

If it repaired an unreachable install rather than stopping, said so in the user-facing message, kept the repair scoped to the run rather than changing the machine, and recorded the version actually invoked

_assertion_kinds.discriminator: Showed a delta between configurations in iteration 1. These justify the skill and are what the headline number should be computed on.
_assertion_kinds.unproven: Passed in BOTH configurations, once. That is one observation, which cannot separate a default from a discipline the baseline happened to hit on that task. Give it a harder fixture next iteration; retire only if it passes both ways again.
_assertion_kinds.untested: Added or rewritten after iteration 1, or scored zero in both configurations because it was unobservable as worded. Grade these first.
